content: Trade data recorded in April 2026 further illustrates the dynamic nature of this sector, showing that South Africa actively engages in both the import and export of prepared explosives [31] . While these trade figures confirm the country's integration into the global explosives supply chain, the highly specialized nature of the market necessitates a reliance on dominant domestic manufacturers to ensure supply chain resilience. This overall decreasing trend across the industry may indicate a strategic shift toward supply chain optimization, wherein suppliers are consolidating their distribution footprints to enhance operational efficiencies, reduce overhead costs, and centralize their safety and compliance monitoring protocols. Fewer, highly advanced distribution centers can often provide better security and stricter adherence to the rigorous safety standards required for the storage and transportation of explosive materials. Despite the critical importance of these logistical frameworks, highly detailed public disclosures regarding the operational specifics of ANFO distribution networks in South Africa between 2024 and 2026 remain limited. Much of the available intelligence is drawn from broader trends in the industrial chemicals and explosives markets. For instance, global reports project significant growth in ammonium nitrate explosives markets, forecasting an increase from 12,660.79 million USD in 2026 to 15,536.22 million USD by the year 2035 [34] . While these global forecasts underscore a strong future demand profile for ANFO and related blasting agents, they do not explicitly detail the localized infrastructural adaptations occurring within South Africa. Similarly, long-term global ANFO blasting sales market projections extending toward 2033 emphasize future market dynamics but offer limited granularity on regional supply chain mechanics [31] . Nevertheless, the alignment of the dtic's priorities with industrial chemical manufacturing suggests a supportive regulatory environment aimed at bolstering the infrastructure upon which suppliers like AECI, BME, and 35 rely. Efforts to secure resilient distribution networks under evolving global conditions remain a priority in general discussions surrounding ammonium nitrate products, reflecting the industry's continuous adaptation to both market demand and stringent safety compliance requirements [32] .
